The '''2024 FA Community Shield''' was the 102nd [[FA Community Shield]], an annual [[association football]] match contested by the winners of the previous season's [[Premier League]] and [[FA Cup]] competitions. It was played at [[Wembley Stadium]] in London on 10 August 2024,<ref name="details">{{cite news |title=2024 FA Community Shield date, kick-off time and TV details are confirmed |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2024/jun/26/community-shield-date-kick-off-time-confirmed-20242606 |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=26 June 2024 |accessdate=26 June 2024 }}</ref> and featured the [[2023–24 Premier League]] champions [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] and the [[2023–24 FA Cup]] winners [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], who had defeated City in the [[2024 FA Cup final|final]].

[[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] were the holders, having won the [[2023 FA Community Shield|2023 edition]], but they did not qualify for this match, having been knocked out of the FA Cup in the third round and having finished second in the league.

Manchester City beat Manchester United 7–6 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] after a 1–1 draw in normal time, winning their first Community Shield title since [[2019 FA Community Shield|2019]], which they also won on penalties after a 1–1 draw. This was United's first Shield defeat since [[2009 FA Community Shield|2009]], when they were beaten by [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], also on penalties.

==Background==
{{main|2023–24 Manchester City F.C. season|2023–24 Manchester United F.C. season}}
[[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] qualified for the 2024 FA Community Shield as the winners of the [[2023–24 Premier League]] and the [[2023–24 FA Cup]], respectively. It was the 194th [[Manchester derby]] to take place in all competitions and the third to take place in the Community Shield; Manchester United won both previous meetings in [[1956 FA Charity Shield|1956]] (when the competition was known as the Charity Shield) and [[2011 FA Community Shield|2011]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Joe |last=Wright |title=When is the Community Shield 2024? Date and venue for Man City vs. Man United in curtain raiser next season |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/uk/football/news/community-shield-2024-when-date-venue-man-city-man-united/2a16a3570179436981b51674 |work=The Sporting News |date=25 May 2024 |accessdate=26 May 2024 }}</ref>

Manchester United had both appeared in and won the most Community Shield matches, winning 21 of their 30 appearances, although this included four shared titles in [[1965 FA Charity Shield|1965]], [[1967 FA Charity Shield|1967]], [[1977 FA Charity Shield|1977]] and [[1990 FA Charity Shield|1990]]; their most recent title came in [[2016 FA Community Shield|2016]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Leicester City 1–2 Manchester United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36934956 |first=Chris |last=Bevan |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=7 August 2016 |access-date=27 July 2024 |archive-date=21 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321081125/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36934956 |url-status=live }}</ref> Manchester City had appeared in 15 Community Shield matches, winning six titles, the most recent coming in [[2019 FA Community Shield|2019]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool 1–1 Man City (City won 5–4 on pens) |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/49141690 |first=Emlyn |last=Begley |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=4 August 2019 |access-date=27 July 2024 |archive-date=4 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190804155835/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/49141690 |url-status=live }}</ref> It was their fourth Community Shield appearance in a row, with the previous three resulting in defeats, making City the first team to lose three straight Community Shields since United in [[2001 FA Charity Shield|2001]], when they lost a competition record fourth in a row.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool edge out Man Utd |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/1487037.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=12 August 2001 |access-date=27 July 2024 |archive-date=20 April 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080420194953/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/1487037.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Pre-match==
[[File:Wembley_Stadium_prior_to_the_2024_Community_Shield.jpg|thumb|[[Wembley Stadium]] before the game]]
===Officials===
[[John Brooks (referee)|John Brooks]] was originally named as the [[Referee (association football)|referee]] for the Community Shield; however, after Brooks suffered a minor injury in the week before the match, he was replaced by fourth official [[Jarred Gillett]], and Sam Barrott was named as Gillett's replacement. Adrian Holmes and Nick Greenhalgh were named as the [[Assistant referee (association football)|assistant referees]]. The [[video assistant referee]] (VAR) was named as [[Peter Bankes]], with [[Sian Massey-Ellis]] as the assistant VAR and Tim Robinson as the support VAR.<ref name="officials"/>

==Match==
===Summary===
The first half went goalless after City midfielder [[James McAtee]] hit the post with a curling shot and United forward [[Marcus Rashford]] failed to hit the target after being found unmarked in the box. United thought they had opened the scoring early in the second half, when captain [[Bruno Fernandes]] beat [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] with a dipping shot from the edge of the box; however, he was ruled to have been offside in the build-up. Rashford hit the post with just over 15 minutes left after being played in by substitute [[Alejandro Garnacho]], but the Argentine winger opened the scoring seven minutes later, cutting inside off the right wing and beating Ederson with a left-footed strike into the bottom corner. With just under two minutes left in normal time, though, [[Bernardo Silva]] – on his 30th birthday – headed in a cross from [[Oscar Bobb]], forcing the match to go to a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]].<ref name="fa_report">{{cite news |title=Manchester City beat Manchester United on penalties in Community Shield |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2024/aug/10/community-shield-city-united-wrap-20240810 |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=10 August 2024 |accessdate=11 August 2024 }}</ref>

After Fernandes put United 1–0 up in the shoot-out, Silva himself stepped up to take City's first kick, only to see it saved by [[André Onana]]. [[Diogo Dalot]] and Garnacho then scored for United, while [[Kevin De Bruyne]] and [[Erling Haaland]] kept City in it, the score 3–2 after three kicks each. With their fourth attempt, United winger and former [[Manchester City F.C. EDS and Academy|City academy]] player [[Jadon Sancho]] had his penalty saved by Ederson, allowing [[Savinho]] to equalise. After Casemiro scored for United, Ederson himself took City's fifth penalty and scored to take the shoot-out to sudden death. [[Scott McTominay]] and [[Lisandro Martínez]] both scored for United, matched by efforts from [[Matheus Nunes]] and [[Rúben Dias]], but when [[Jonny Evans]] put his kick over the bar, that allowed [[Manuel Akanji]] to score the winning penalty. That gave City their first Community Shield in five years, avoiding the club a joint-record of four consecutive Shield losses, as well as [[Pep Guardiola]]'s third victory in the competition.<ref name="fa_report"/>

==Broadcasting==
The match was broadcast on television in the United Kingdom on [[ITV (TV network)|ITV]] and its on-demand streaming counterparts, [[ITVX]] and [[STV Player]]. On radio, it was broadcast on [[BBC Radio 5 Live]], [[BBC Radio Manchester]], the [[BBC World Service]], [[Talksport]] and Talksport International.<ref name="details"/>
